title: TMD-Bench: A Multi-Level Evaluation Paradigm for Music–Dance Co-Generation
claim: A benchmark combines dataset construction, multi-level evaluation protocol, and metric taxonomy into one framework that ranks diverse models.
layout: 4 quadrant panels, colored borders, top-to-bottom; bar chart and radar plot bottom-right
description: A four-quadrant overview with colored rounded borders. Top-left (blue) shows the dataset construction pipeline as a snaking chain of boxes with small icons: curate dance videos, motion and stability filtering, separate vocals, generate captions, content filtering, quality filtering, human verification, video prompt design. Top-right shows the dataset overview: a sample text prompt, five dancer video frames with an audio waveform below, and a concentric ring chart of dance attributes. Bottom-left (orange) is the model evaluation protocol: a text instruction, a generated video filmstrip, labels for instruction adherence, unimodal quality (high-level and low-level) and cross-modal rhythmic alignment, and a waveform with beat markers. Bottom-right (pink) has a fox and rabbit mascot, a music/video/alignment metric taxonomy with arrows, a horizontal bar chart grouped by closed-source, cascaded and open-source models, and a radar chart.
caption: Overview of TMD-Bench, a benchmark for text-driven music–dance co-generation. The top-left panel illustrates the dataset construction pipeline. The dataset overview (top-right) shows the distribution of dance-related attributes in the 10k dataset; each concentric ring corresponds to an attribute—Performer Cardinality, Dance Style Category, Performer Attributes, and Scene Context (from inner to outer). The evaluation protocol (bottom-left) assesses models across (I) instruction adherence, (II) unimodal generation quality, and (III) cross-modal rhythmic alignment. The bottom-right summarizes the TMD-Bench metric taxonomy covering music, video, and alignment, along with comparative performance across closed-source, cascaded, and open-source models.
abstract: Unified audio-visual generation is rapidly gaining industrial and creative relevance, enabling applications in virtual production and interactive media. However, when moving from general audio-video synthesis to music-dance co-generation, the task becomes substantially harder: musical rhythm, phrasing, and accents must drive choreographic motion at fine temporal resolution, and such rhythmic coupling is not captured by unimodal metrics or generic audiovisual consistency scores used in current evaluation practice. We introduce TMD-Bench, a benchmark for text-driven music-dance co-generation that assesses systems across unimodal generation quality, instruction adherence, and cross-modal rhythmic alignment. The benchmark integrates computable physical metrics with perceptual multimodal judgments, and is supported by a curated rhythm-aligned music-dance dataset and a fine-grained Music Captioner for structured music semantics. TMD-Bench further reveals that (i) modern commercial audio-visual models, such as Veo 3 and Sora 2, produce high-quality music and video, while rhythmic coupling remains less consistently optimized and leaves room for improvement, and (ii) our unified baseline RhyJAM trained on rhythm-aligned data achieves competitive beat-level synchronization while maintaining competitive unimodal fidelity. This presents prospects for building next-generation music-dance models that explicitly optimize rhythmic and kinetic coherence.
